archetype.name: Gunslinger (pocket-bound)
archetype.definition: An accurate, aggressive pocket thrower who wins with tight-window throws and the intermediate-to-deep game, and has always paid for it in interceptions.

report.headline: Accurate arm undone by sacks, picks and third-and-long so far
report.take:
Darnold arrived in 2026 off two strong seasons. His EPA per play ranked 20th in 2024 and 14th in 2025, his CPOE was top-10 both years, and his yards per attempt ranked 8th and 5th. The same two seasons also show who he has always been: his interception totals ranked 50th of 60 and 61st of 63. He is a rhythm passer who will make the hard throw, and every year some of those throws go the other way.

This season is really three full starts, since he played 10% of the snaps in Week 1. The team's start log credits Drew Lock with Weeks 2-5, but Darnold's own log has him on every snap in Weeks 3-5, and he is listed as QB1. One of those starts was excellent: 379 yards and four touchdowns against Washington, now the 24th-ranked defense. The other two came against the 6th- and 4th-ranked defenses and produced 8 sacks, 3 interceptions and -17.2 combined EPA. All of his sacks and interceptions came in one-score situations, where his EPA per play is -0.325. The supporting cast explains much of that. The run game ranks 30th in EPA, which leaves him an average of 8.3 yards to go on third down, and he converts 24.1% of them. He is hit or sacked on 20.6% of dropbacks behind a line whose QB-hit rate ranks 29th.

What the -0.142 EPA hides is that the throwing itself has held up. His bad-throw rate of 5.1% is the lowest among 36 qualifiers. He is positive in both intermediate EPA (+0.235) and deep EPA (+0.621, on only 10 attempts). The losses come from the short and screen game: throws behind the line are completed 80% of the time yet return -0.467 EPA. They also come from targets outside his top two. Smith-Njigba and Kupp are clearly positive per target, while Barner (-0.546 on 17 targets) and Shaheed (-0.424 on 11) have been drains. He is holding the ball 3.25 seconds, up from 2.87 last year, and still throwing short of the sticks. That suggests nothing is open downfield rather than a quarterback who is scared of it. On the other side, six red-zone touchdowns on 15 attempts with no interceptions is flattering his TD rate, and that will cool.

The interceptions are the part to believe. The career says they are part of the package, though a 5.1% rate is above even his usual level. The efficiency collapse is the part to doubt: it rests on about 110 dropbacks, two of them games against elite defenses. Expect his EPA to climb back toward slightly positive, though the protection and the run game cap how far.

strengths.title: Ball placement remains top-tier
strengths.body: His bad-throw rate is the best among qualifiers and his CPOE is positive, so the misses are not inaccuracy. That matches 2024-25, when his CPOE ranked 10th and 9th. This is a durable skill, not a hot streak.

strengths.title: Wins in the intermediate and deep game
strengths.body: When he pushes the ball past 10 yards, the offense works: +0.235 EPA on intermediate throws with a 66.7% success rate, and +0.621 on deep shots. The deep number rests on 10 attempts and will come down. The intermediate success fits his career profile as a strong middle-of-the-field passer.

strengths.title: Two reliable targets
strengths.body: Smith-Njigba (29 targets, +0.343 per target) and Kupp (+0.485 on 10) are the offense's efficient options. When the ball goes their way, Darnold's numbers look like his 2025 self, which makes their availability central to his outlook.

concerns.title: Interceptions, as always, plus more
concerns.body: Five picks on 98 attempts is a 5.1% rate, 40th of 43, and all five were charted turnover-worthy. Interceptions have been the constant of his career, including a 61st-of-63 ranking in his best season, so the rate should ease but the problem will not go away.

concerns.title: Protection and run game create long downs
concerns.body: A line ranked 29th in QB-hit rate and a run game ranked 30th leave him in third-and-long, where his EPA is -0.459. His pressure-to-sack rate is actually decent (8th), so the sacks reflect volume more than holding the ball. With Charbonnet out, that is unlikely to change soon.

concerns.title: Short and screen game is dead weight
concerns.body: Throws behind the line return -0.467 EPA despite 80% completions, and short throws are negative with a -4 CPOE. Barner's -0.546 per target on 17 looks is a big part of it. That points to scheme and personnel more than the quarterback, but it drags on every drive.

trend.note: His pass EPA went from +4.1 to -5.2 to -12 across his three full starts, but the opponents went from the 24th-ranked defense to the 6th and 4th. The slide tracks the schedule as much as the player.

nextGame.headline: Elite Denver pass defense, minus both starting corners, on a short week
nextGame.body:
On paper Denver is the third toughest pass defense he could face: 3rd in pass EPA, 4th in deep EPA and 5th in QB-hit rate. That is the profile that sacked and picked him against the Chargers and 49ers. The opening is underneath. Denver ranks 24th in short-pass EPA, sends 24.3% of opponents' targets to running backs against an 18.2% league share, and ranks 28th against the run. That gives Seattle an easier path than usual on early downs. It's a Thursday road game on four days' rest.

Availability tilts this. Pat Surtain II and Riley Moss are both out, removing two starting corners who each played close to 90% of snaps. Safety Talanoa Hufanga, a 93% player, missed Monday's practice and is questionable. That should soften the deep coverage that drives Denver's rankings. On Seattle's side, Smith-Njigba, his best target by volume, is questionable with an ankle injury after a limited practice. Without him, more targets go to Barner and Shaheed, the two players losing EPA. Drew Lock (forearm) is questionable, which matters only as depth since Darnold practiced fully.

keyMatchups.title: Depleted Broncos secondary vs intermediate game
keyMatchups.body: Denver's 4th-ranked deep EPA was built with Surtain and Moss, and both are out. Darnold's best work comes from 10+ yards, so this is the window where his EPA could swing positive if the protection holds.

keyMatchups.title: Denver pass rush vs Seattle's line
keyMatchups.body: Denver ranks 5th in QB-hit rate and 10th in sack rate, against a Seattle line ranked 29th in QB hits allowed. He took 8 sacks in his two games against top defenses, so getting the ball out early is the game.

keyMatchups.title: Soft underneath, leaky against the run
keyMatchups.body: Denver is 24th in short-pass EPA and funnels targets to backs, which fits the check-down plan Seattle needs. If Holani and the run game can exploit a 28th-ranked run defense, third downs shorten, and that has been his biggest problem.

nextGame.watch: Whether Smith-Njigba plays, and whether Seattle's early-down calls keep Darnold out of third-and-8 against Denver's rush.

restOfSeason.body:
The base case is a rebound toward his 2024-25 level, not all the way to it. The accuracy, the intermediate game and the top two targets are real and carried over from his career. The -0.142 EPA rests on three full starts, two of them against top-six defenses. What won't fully fix itself is the environment: a bottom-three run game, a line that allows hits and no Charbonnet push him into obvious passing downs. That keeps sacks near three a game against good fronts.

The touchdown rate (6th) and red-zone perfection will regress, and so should the 5.1% interception rate, though his history says picks stay above league norms. Expect solid yardage, around two touchdowns per full game that drifts lower, and close to one interception a week.
swingFactors: Whether the run game can get off the bottom with Charbonnet out

bets.reason: He has thrown a pick in all three full starts (2, 1, 2), his INT rate is 40th of 43, and his career shows interceptions follow him even in good years. Denver's defense ranks 3rd against the pass and 5th in QB-hit rate; the missing corners are the only thing pulling against this.
He took 8 sacks against the two good defenses he faced, behind a line 29th in QB hits allowed. Denver ranks 5th in hit rate and 10th in sack rate, and a short-week road game rarely helps protection.

Seattle's defense ranks 2nd in EPA against a Denver offense ranked 24th. Denver is without both starting corners for Darnold's best area of the field. The risk is Darnold's turnovers and Seattle's run of no covers (two pushes, two losses).

confidence.note: Three full starts, two against elite defenses, and a muddled start log, but a strong two-year career baseline anchors the read.
